scenes.vo: In March twenty twenty-six, Adobe agreed to a one hundred fifty million dollar settlement over its subscriptions.

visual.note: $75M civil penalty + $75M in free services for customers (U.S. Justice Department)

scenes.vo: At its center: a cancellation fee one executive called a bit like heroin for Adobe. Why?

visual.who: An Adobe executive, quoted in the U.S. complaint (2024). Adobe says the remark was taken out of context.

scenes.vo: Creative Cloud cost eighty-two forty-nine a month. Or fifty-four ninety-nine on the annual, paid monthly plan, often the default.

visual.headline:
SAME APPS,
TWO PRICES
visual.source: Per month · Adobe often preselected the annual plan (U.S. complaint)

scenes.vo: But that plan is a one-year contract. Cancel early, and you're charged half of what's left.

visual.note: Early termination fee if you cancel in year one. Example: 6 months left = $329.94 → fee $164.97

scenes.vo: Adobe says these fees were under half a percent of its revenue. So what's the prize?

visual.sub:
OF ADOBE'S REVENUE
CAME FROM THESE FEES
visual.note: Adobe general counsel Dana Rao, July 2024

scenes.vo: The lock: twelve months of payments from customers who signed up for a monthly price.
A cancellation fee doesn't need to make money. It makes leaving cost more than staying.

visual.display: A cancellation fee doesn't need to make money. It makes *leaving* cost more than *staying.*
